content: Firestore security rules docs (fetched 2026-08-06): VERBATIM — 'security rules are not filters—queries are all or nothing... If a query could potentially return documents that the client does not have permission to read, the entire request fails.' Every collection query MUST be scoped by the uid equality filter matching the rule (e.g. where('uid','==',uid)) or the whole query fails with permission-denied even for the user's own data. Individual doc gets (doc(id)) evaluate rules per doc — safe. This project's backend-schema.md lists query patterns WITHOUT uid filters (e.g. where type=='expense', date-range queries) — those will fail under the documented rules; every query needs the uid clause added. Rules are not evaluated on cached reads while offline (already-authorized data is served from cache); offline writes bypass rules until sync.
